chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn: that he wrote to him asking about a man who married a woman in one of the towns.

So he asked her, 'Do you have a husband?' She said, 'No,' so he married her. Then a man came to him and said, 'She is my wife.' The woman denied that, saying it does not bind the husband. He said, 'She is his wife unless he produces evidence.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries a woman who says she is single, but another man later claims she is his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in marital status, where the initial marriage is presumed valid until proven otherwise. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the burden of proof (*al-bayyina 'ala al-mud'i*) falling upon the claimant of a prior or competing marriage, ensuring legal stability in family law.
